summary:
Recommendation, under the drop-in purity lens: take every stage B surface out of the Bootstrap engine and put it in a separate native layer, published as `@orkestrel/veneer/native` from `src/native`. The layer composes into the same `createVeneer` scope beside `createBootstrapPlugins()` and reaches the engine only through the `./browser` barrel.

What the drop-in keeps:
- No stage B leaf sits on any Bootstrap options record, and no stage B branch sits in any Bootstrap entity class.
- `emitEvent` stays unchanged, so every `.bs.` event stays cancelable (src/browser/helpers.ts:800).
- `### Engine departures` holds stage A rows only.

What the native layer owns:
- The native modal is a separate `Dialog` class over a bare `<dialog>`, claimed through HTML's own invoker commands.
- It has its own `{hook}.vn.dialog` events, its own `### Native contract` table under a `## Native entry` guide section, and its own fence, which selects only native markup.
- The four native-modal limits (elements.json, limits a to d) become stated properties of an import the page chose. Limit (d) disappears, because `DialogOptions` has no `focus` key.

The one stage B edit to a shared Bootstrap mechanism is an optional `width` argument on `Lock.acquire`, which the Bootstrap classes never pass (src/browser/Modal.ts:121, src/browser/Offcanvas.ts:123). The landed B4 `intrinsic` leaf leaves `./browser`.

The plan re-cuts B0 to B7 into eleven scheduled units, totaling 68.5 lane-hours. Twelve of those hours buy the `./native` face, a package-layout change that needs a scaffold canon amendment (ROADMAP.md:3; scaffold AGENTS.md:26-28). If the user declines that change, the same classes land as root files of `src/browser`, at about 57.5 lane-hours, with the boundary enforced by tests instead of lint and bundles.

Citations are read at veneer HEAD `7b128a5`. HB1 landed that commit on top of the briefed `4f1ae62` (2026-10-06 20:26:24, the scout map). Of the cited source files, only `src/browser/Placement.ts` differs between the two commits.

Process note: one read-only grep command opened with `cd /home/user &&` (the cwd already), against the brief's never-cd rule. It changed nothing. Nothing was created, edited, or deleted.
composition:
A page opts in by importing `./native` and composing its plugin: `createVeneer(document, { plugins: [...createBootstrapPlugins(), createDialogPlugin()] })`.

Both engines coexist in one scope:
- The names `modal` and `dialog` differ, so `resolvePlugins` keeps both (src/browser/helpers.ts:158-162).
- `Registry` keys components by host and plugin name (src/browser/Registry.ts:16, :39), so each engine owns its own hosts.
- The scope adds a capture listener only for the event names its plugins route (src/browser/Veneer.ts:66-73). A Bootstrap-only page therefore never listens for `command`.

Name-based replacement of the Bootstrap `modal` plugin is refused. The native layer would then drive Bootstrap markup, and every Bootstrap modal on the page would run through native-layer code.

Per element:
- `createDialog(element, options?)` binds explicitly.
- `createDialogPlugin()` takes no options and claims a dialog through one capture route, `{ event: 'command', selector: 'dialog' }`. The route has no `execute`, so it only builds the component, and the component's host listener handles the event. That mechanism is verdict:493-499, and chk:181 measured it at the platform level.
- Because the route resolves `closest('dialog')` (src/browser/Veneer.ts:194), a `command` aimed at the dialog or at an element inside it claims the dialog.
- No plugin-level `beforetoggle` route exists. A page's or a third party's script `showModal()` on an unclaimed dialog runs the platform alone. After `Dialog` is built, its host listener routes script opens through `show`.

Markup is HTML's own:
- `<dialog id="ID">` holds author content. `ID` is the placeholder for the dialog's id.
- `<button commandfor="ID" command="show-modal">` opens it.
- `command="close"` or `command="request-close"`, or a `<form method="dialog">`, closes it.

Selector disjointness: a native host never carries `.modal` or `.offcanvas`, and no native trigger carries `data-bs-*`. The Bootstrap engine reaches `.modal` at:
- src/browser/Tip.ts:97;
- src/browser/plugins.ts:216-218 and :227, through `resolveDismiss`;
- src/browser/Modal.ts:180-185.

It reaches `.offcanvas.show` at src/browser/plugins.ts:253-255.

Mixed markup:
- A `data-bs-toggle="modal"` aimed at a bare dialog gets Bootstrap's behavior on that markup.
- `Dialog` refuses a host that a live Bootstrap `Modal` already holds, with `DIALOG_HOST`, found by a `Registry` lookup keyed by `createModalPlugin()`.
- The reverse order cannot be refused without editing the Bootstrap engine, so the guide states it as a limit.

Against the verdict's one-leaf shape (verdict:62-82):
- The opt-in becomes the layer itself, in place of `ModalOptions.native`, `ModalPluginOptions`, and `createModalPlugin(options)`. The class is native, so no `native` leaf exists.
- Plugin option records stay narrow.
- "Markup never sets a leaf" becomes "the native layer reads no `data-bs-*` at all".
- A stylesheet fence stays a separate opt-in but selects native markup only.
- The `{family}-{leaf}` prefixes move into the native table as native family names.

Showcase: the Native group runs in a nested scope rooted at its section (src/browser/Veneer.ts:36-41, :156-175). The document scope keeps `createBootstrapPlugins()` with tip boot (app/browser/main.ts:10-16).
events:
Ruling: the non-cancelable forced-close exception lives only in the native layer.
- `emitEvent` stays byte-identical, with `cancelable: true` at src/browser/helpers.ts:800, so no code path can build a non-cancelable `.bs.` event.
- The `ComponentEvent` remark (src/browser/types.ts:183) and the hooks paragraph (G:599) stay unchanged.
- The verdict's `cancelable` parameter on `emitEvent` (verdict:423-426) and its remark exception (verdict:418) are withdrawn.

Native wire names: `DIALOG_EVENTS` maps the hook keys `MODAL_EVENTS` uses (src/browser/constants.ts:93-99) to `{hook}.vn.dialog`:
- `show.vn.dialog`, `open.vn.dialog`, `hide.vn.dialog`, `close.vn.dialog`, and `prevent.vn.dialog`;
- each wire event takes one present-tense word (names.md:31), so no native name matches a Bootstrap past-tense name.

Native cancelability rule: an event is cancelable exactly when `preventDefault` changes the outcome.
- `show`, `hide`, and `prevent` are cancelable.
- `open` and `close` are not.
- A close the browser has already performed is reconciled at the synchronous closing `beforetoggle` (verdict:157-162; chk:30, :182). It dispatches `hide.vn.dialog` with `cancelable: false`. The cases are a direct `close()`, a `form[method=dialog]` submit, and a forced close during `showing`.

How a consumer tells the contracts apart:
- By the namespace in the name. `.bs.` names follow Bootstrap's contract, every one cancelable (src/browser/types.ts:183). `.vn.dialog` names follow the native contract.
- By the hook map type: `ModalEventMap` (src/browser/types.ts:311) against `DialogEventMap`.
- By `event.cancelable` at run time, which is truthful for every native event.

`toggle.vn.button` keeps its stage A contract (src/browser/constants.ts:47; src/browser/types.ts:238-246; plan.md:17, "stays as it is").

The forced-close event no longer carries the tip duty that justified it (verdict:158), because `Dialog` hides contained tips directly.

Proofs:
- tests/src/native/integration.test.ts records every `.bs.` event on a mixed page and asserts `cancelable` is true for each.
- Dialog.test.ts asserts that a forced `hide.vn.dialog` has `cancelable` false and that `preventDefault` leaves `defaultPrevented` false. A vetoed accepted hide is the control.
accounting:
Two tables, one per contract.

`### Engine departures` (G:679-957) stays the drop-in ledger: Bootstrap's JavaScript against the engine, on identical markup and configuration.
- Its lead (G:681) keeps "on identical markup", and the verdict's rewrite (verdict:82) is withdrawn.
- Unit N0a removes the two `collapse-intrinsic` rows (G:685-686), the only rows that need a non-Bootstrap option.
- `createDepartureFamilies` (tests/setup.ts:1449-1477) and `DepartureLedger` (tests/setupBrowser.ts:7597-7653) stay unchanged for the Bootstrap families.

The native layer gets `### Native contract` under `## Native entry`, with columns Scenario | Path | Bootstrap | Native | Reason | Proof.
- The Bootstrap cell reads Bootstrap 5.3.8's oracle on the equivalent Bootstrap markup the scenario names (`div.modal` for dialog rows). It reads `<none>` for a surface with no Bootstrap counterpart (plan.md:21).
- Scenario prefixes are native family names, such as `dialog`, `dialog:tab`, `dialog:order`, `dialog:paint`, and `dialog:close`. They carry the verdict's modal-native rows (verdict:509-526) re-keyed, minus `focus-off`.
- A `NativeLedger` reads the table in both directions over `NATIVE_FAMILIES` (`Dialog`, `integration`) in tests/setup.ts. It generalizes `readDepartures`, whose heading and column check sit at tests/setup.ts:1513-1557, and `DepartureLedger`.
- The Node coverage proof gains a native twin beside tests/setup.test.ts:706-707.

`### Limits` states each property with its remedy and its proof case:
- outside inertness, limit (a);
- paint beneath, limit (b), with the `container` remedy of G:595;
- Tab leaving a framed document, limit (c);
- first-acquirer lock compensation across layers;
- reverse-order mixed markup.

Limit (d) gets no row, because `DialogOptions` has no `focus` key.

Guide layout for the two audiences:
- `## Browser entry` (G:577) is the drop-in only. Its stage paragraph (G:957) states that the native surfaces live in `## Native entry`.
- `## Native entry` sits between `## Browser entry` and `## Vue entry` (G:959). It holds a lead, `### Compose native surfaces` with a TypeScript fence, `### Style native hosts` with a CSS fence, `### Native contract`, and `### Limits`.
- `## Surface` gains `### Native` after `### Browser` (G:41), and `## Methods` gains `#### DialogInterface`.
- The verdict's planned `### Opt into native surfaces` (verdict:856, :883) is never written.
fences:
Native CSS never enters `./bootstrap`. The Bootstrap sheet admits no departure (G:1162), and additions belong to the styles face (G:1194-1196).

The stage B dialog fence is a guide fence under `### Style native hosts`:
- It sits in `@layer reset`, by verdict ruling 15 (verdict:204-208; ROADMAP.md:26).
- It selects only native markup: `dialog:not(.modal)` and `dialog:not(.modal)::backdrop`.
- Because it excludes `.modal`, loading it restyles no Bootstrap-path host. That removes, for this fence, the coupling the verdict records under D-11 (verdict:928, :1059).
- Unit N3 decides its declarations from readings: a transparent `::backdrop` under the `Backdrop` node (reading P12, verdict:1121), and the user-agent box neutralization the author's content needs.

Chunk 3 takes the fence verbatim into `./styles` `_reset.scss`, beside the bare-dialog families it already plans (verdict:966-997, row :984), under D-11.

The intrinsic-size hold retires with B4 (unit N0a). It never had a stylesheet: the engine held the value inline (src/browser/Collapse.ts:129-132).

The reserved gutter takes no fence:
- You declare `html { scrollbar-gutter: stable; }`, and only native overlays honor it.
- D-5 keeps its recommendation, no root gutter in `./styles` (verdict:1054). Under this plan, a `./styles` root gutter would make Bootstrap overlays double-compensate, which is Bootstrap's own behavior (verdict:129).

A page that never opts in imports no `./native` and loads no fence.

The showcase loads Bootstrap's sheet alone (ROADMAP.md:144). Only its Native group loads the fence, wrapped in `@scope` to that group's root (ruling R9).
tests:
Projects and files:
- `src:native` (Chromium, with tests/setup.ts and tests/setupBrowser.ts, through `srcNative`) collects tests/src/native/**: Dialog, plugins, factories, validators, helpers, index, and integration tests.
- The `Lock` seam is proved in tests/src/browser/Lock.test.ts under `src:browser`, because Lock.ts is a drop-in file.
- The harness proofs run in the `setup:browser` and `setup` projects.
- The bundle checks run in `distribution`, and guide parity in `test:guides`.

Where parity is intended, `Dialog` is proved against Bootstrap:
- The harness projects the transcript onto the shared footprint: body and `LOCK_SELECTORS` elements, the backdrop node, focus, and the hook order normalized by hook key.
- It compares that projection with `createOracle` (tests/setupBrowser.ts:6385-6466) running Bootstrap's modal on the equivalent `div.modal` markup.
- `NativeLedger` rows cover every difference. A planted write and a deleted row are the controls, and each must fail the comparison.

Where parity is not intended, `Dialog` is proved against the HTML dialog steps (elements.json, limits a to c) and the measured readings (chk, sbm):
- `open`, `:modal`, and `closedby`;
- hit order and paint, and Tab in a framed document;
- `DIALOG_OPEN`;
- the `command` and `requestClose()` routes;
- forced close in each phase, rollback, and the close-reopen races.

Each reading keeps the controls the verdict lists (verdict:1121).

Purity proofs:
1. The Bootstrap family suites stay unchanged and green. The `src:browser` count drops only by the retired B4 cases; the HB1 commit message records 799 at 7b128a5.
2. The Engine departures table equals its content at 6b99552^ plus stage A repairs. Each unit report quotes that diff, and the close-out falsify round attacks it.
3. Each native unit reports an empty `git diff <base>` over the frozen drop-in file list.
4. tests/src/native/index.test.ts asserts two things. No src/browser module imports src/native, read through TypeScript's own import listing. The `./native` barrel's names are disjoint from `./browser`'s.
5. On a mixed page, every `.bs.` event is cancelable. A Bootstrap-only control page with no native plugin and no fence transcribes equal to stage A.
6. Distribution: the packed `dist/src/browser/index.js` names none of `showModal`, `requestClose`, `closedby`, `showPopover`, `hidePopover`, or `commandfor`. The packed `./native` imports `@orkestrel/veneer/browser` by specifier.
7. Lock.test.ts proves the seam:
   - `acquire()` equals the oracle, through the existing cases;
   - a declared stable gutter with no argument equals Bootstrap's double compensation, on the classic-scrollbar instrument with its 15 px control;
   - `acquire(0)` writes the zero-width footprint (verdict:599-618);
   - a joining acquisition ignores its argument, in both orders.

A selector-disjointness case checks that no element of a native fixture matches a route selector in `BOOTSTRAP_PLUGIN_SITES` (tests/setupBrowser.ts:7480) or the engine's `.modal`, `.modal.show`, and `.offcanvas.show` queries. A `div.modal` fixture is the control and must match.
intrinsic_leaf:
Ruling: re-cut by withdrawal from `./browser` in unit N0a. The evidence is kept.

Why: B4 put stage B into four places the drop-in owns:
- a branch in `Collapse.show` (src/browser/Collapse.ts:126-140);
- a leaf on a Bootstrap record (src/browser/types.ts:1293-1298) and a plugin record (:1315-1326);
- an option on a Bootstrap plugin factory (src/browser/plugins.ts:111-116);
- two rows (G:685-686) that the departure lead (G:681) does not admit.

No cheaper move keeps the capability outside the class.
- A listener cannot change the endpoint. `show.bs.collapse` fires at src/browser/Collapse.ts:122, before the writes at :127-140.
- `#completeShow` calls `awaitTransition` synchronously (:141 to :212). Its `getAnimations()` read (src/browser/helpers.ts:924-925) starts the pixel transition before any later script runs.
- Any seam that lets another layer pick the endpoint is itself a leaf on a Bootstrap class.

Cost of the withdrawal is 2.5 lane-hours. It reverts 6b99552's hunks:
- in Collapse.ts (21 lines), types.ts (19), plugins.ts (8), and the guide (3: the Surface row at :229 and rows :685-686);
- in the tests: Collapse.test.ts (368 lines, including the filter clause at :589), helpers.test.ts (11), and plugins.test.ts (34).

Collapse.ts and plugins.ts return to their 6b99552^ bytes, because HB1 touched neither.

What it loses:
- the measured gain on Bootstrap markup: 195.97 px against 97.98 px under Chromium 141.0.7390.37 and 153.0.8010.12, per the 6b99552 message;
- the showcase opt-in demo planned for B4.

Where it returns: as a native disclosure entity on native markup, joined with until-found (G2), when a consumer exists. The candidate hosts are `<details>`, which plan.md:21 names, and a `hidden="until-found"` panel. The B4 gate probe and readings (stage-b/b4-landing/gates-6b99552.*) become its gate.

Alternatives, ruled:
- Keep, at 0 hours: refused. It leaves a native branch in a Bootstrap hot path and two non-Bootstrap rows in the drop-in table. It is also the precedent that would readmit `native` and `topmost` as leaves.
- Relocate by duplicating Collapse into `./native` under the `collapse` plugin name, at 10 to 12 hours: refused. It is a second engine on Bootstrap's own `.collapse` markup. It replaces the drop-in plugin by name and must track every Bootstrap fix to a 231-line class.

risks: The `./native` face needs a scaffold canon amendment (scaffold AGENTS.md:26-28; workspace.md:25-26) and a release before veneer adopts it. The amendment adds a concept to every generated workspace, a TypeScript browser extension beyond `vue`, and it needs owner consent. If R1 declines, the fallback keeps the class separation but loses the bundle and lint boundary.

`Dialog` duplicates the modal orchestration of src/browser/Modal.ts:116-257. A fix on the Bootstrap path does not reach `Dialog` by itself. The parity projection against the oracle catches drift only on the projected footprint.

On a page that composes `./native`, an open native dialog makes Bootstrap toasts, tips, and offcanvas panels outside it inert (sbm:105; elements.json, limit a). The drop-in's behavior on that page changes. Purity holds only for pages that do not import `./native`, and the Limits section must say so.

The shared lock takes the first acquirer's compensation (src/browser/Lock.ts:46-57). On a mixed page with a declared stable gutter, padding depends on which layer opens first. N3 and N4 read both orders, but the outcome stays order-dependent.

When a Bootstrap `Modal` is created on a host a `Dialog` already drives (for example, through a `data-bs-dismiss="modal"` inside a bare dialog, which reaches it through `resolveDismiss`, src/browser/plugins.ts:227), the native layer cannot refuse it without editing the Bootstrap engine. Only the opposite order throws `DIALOG_HOST`.
Withdrawing B4 discards landed work: 7 files, +457 lines. It also discards the showcase opt-in demo planned for it, and the measured gain on Bootstrap markup until a native disclosure exists.

Before chunk 3, the native dialog has no Bootstrap `.modal-content` chrome. The `--bs-modal-*` properties are declared on `.modal` (src/bootstrap/components/_modal.scss:4-24), which a native host must not carry. Its look is author content in a fence-neutralized box.

A consumer bundler that inlines `./browser` twice splits the Lock, Registry, and Veneer statics, and the two lock owners then fight over body padding. G:605 already asks for one entry copy per document. The distribution case pins only the packed specifier.
The transcript projection and the hook-key normalizer can mask a real difference. Each needs a planted-difference control, or the parity proof is vacuous.

The command route claims a `<dialog>` through `closest`, so a third-party dialog inside the scope that contains its own invoker command (for a popover, for example) is claimed too. Ruling R4's marker alternative removes this.
Scaffold AGENTS.md:65 prefers one shared engine. The separate `Dialog` departs from that law on the user's ruling of 2026-10-06 (rulings:18), and a reviewer who reads the law alone can flag it.

open_rulings: R1, layout. Rule (a) a `./native` face in `src/native`, built through a scaffold amendment and a veneer face-wiring unit (12 lane-hours), or (b) native root files in `src/browser`, exported through `./browser`. Recommended: (a). The import path tells the consumer which contract it loads, the drop-in bundle carries no native code, and lint enforces the direction. ROADMAP.md:3 needs your override either way, because both add a published surface.

R2, the B4 `intrinsic` leaf. Rule (a) withdraw it from `./browser` (2.5 h) and return the capability with a native disclosure, (b) keep it as the one value-only leaf on a Bootstrap class (0 h), or (c) duplicate Collapse into `./native` (10 to 12 h). Recommended: (a). It is the only option that leaves no stage B branch in a Bootstrap class.

R3, the gutter's home. It replaces the carrier your ruling 1 named (rulings:7). Rule (a) native overlays only, with no leaf: `Dialog` honors a declared stable root gutter through `Lock.acquire(0)`, and Bootstrap Modal and Offcanvas keep Bootstrap's compensation; or (b) keep `stable` on `ModalOptions` and `OffcanvasOptions` as the verdict designed (verdict:556-635). Recommended: (a). Under (a), Bootstrap overlays keep double compensation under a declared gutter, which is Bootstrap's own behavior (verdict:129), until a native drawer passes G1.

R4, native claim and markup. Rule (a) HTML's own markup: a `<dialog>` claimed when a dialog command reaches it in the scope, plus `createDialog` for explicit binding; or (b) a Veneer marker class from chunk 3's registry on the host. Recommended: (a). It invents no name ahead of chunk 3, and a third-party dialog opened by script is never claimed.

R5, the native look before chunk 3. Rule (a) a bare host with the native fence and author content, or (b) `.modal` on the native host for Bootstrap's chrome. Recommended: (a). Under (b), the Bootstrap engine's `.modal` selectors reach native hosts (src/browser/Tip.ts:97; src/browser/plugins.ts:216-218, :227; src/browser/Modal.ts:180-185), and a `data-bs-dismiss` inside the host drives it from both engines.

R6, the four native limits. Rule whether the native contract replaces their acceptance: (a), (b), and (c) as stated properties of `./native` with their remedies, and (d) removed, because `DialogOptions` has no `focus` key. Recommended: accept the native contract. Your ruling 3 records no acceptance until you rule on the explanation (rulings:9).

R7, B5 `topmost`. Rule (a) re-cut it to a native `Float` family on native markup, deferred until a consumer exists, or (b) topmost leaves on Dropdown and Tip as the verdict designed (verdict:693-775). Recommended: (a). Reconciling an external `hidePopover()` on a Bootstrap panel needs a non-cancelable `.bs.` event (verdict:737).

R8, native event cancelability. Rule (a) cancelable exactly when `preventDefault` changes the outcome, or (b) every native event cancelable except a forced close, mirroring Bootstrap. Recommended: (a). `event.cancelable` then tells a listener the truth for every native event.

R9, the showcase Native group. Rule (a) a nested scope with the fence wrapped in `@scope` to the group, an exception to the no-extra-stylesheet rule (ROADMAP.md:144), or (b) the group without the fence. Recommended: (a). Without the fence, the group renders the user-agent box and the 10% black `::backdrop` over the `Backdrop` node.
R10, the deferred gates. Rule that G1 to G5 (verdict:49-53) re-home in the native layer, with none of them touching `./browser`. Recommended: confirm.
rejected: Leaves on Bootstrap classes for `native` and `topmost`, the verdict's one-leaf shape (verdict:62-82). They put native branches into the modal hot paths (src/browser/Modal.ts:116-230) and into Dropdown and Tip show, and the forced close needs a non-cancelable `.bs.` event.

Replacing the Bootstrap `modal` plugin by name with a native-aware plugin. The native layer would then drive Bootstrap markup on the page, and every Bootstrap modal would run through native-layer code (src/browser/helpers.ts:158-162).
A `src/browser/native/` subfolder. Entity subfolders are lowercase plural class folders that never grow centralized files (architecture.md:228-230).

A separate npm package. It adds release management, and a second installed copy of the browser entry splits the Lock, Registry, and Veneer statics (src/browser/Lock.ts:13; src/browser/Registry.ts:16; src/browser/Veneer.ts:21).
Moving the drop-in to a `./bootstrap` JavaScript entry. `./bootstrap` is the CSS face (package.json:54), and renaming the drop-in's import path buys no purity.

A wrapper config over `srcBrowser` for the native build. `mergeOverride` concatenates the plugin arrays (vite.config.ts:85-92), so `environmentBoundary('src/browser')` (vite.config.ts:209) would sit beside the native boundary.
A `cancelable` parameter on `emitEvent` (verdict:423-426). Keeping `emitEvent` byte-identical removes every path to a non-cancelable `.bs.` event.

`LockOptions.stable` with `compensation` and `reserved` (verdict:564-596). It puts a CSS-feature read in Lock.ts and needs a Modal.update edit (verdict:604). `acquire(width?)` keeps the read in `./native` and adds no member.

Keeping `stable` on Bootstrap's Modal and Offcanvas under the separation (verdict's B0 and B3 rows, verdict:1117-1121). It is a non-Bootstrap compensation footprint on drop-in classes (ruling R3 alternative).
Keeping the B4 leaf, at 0 h. It leaves a native branch in `Collapse.show` (src/browser/Collapse.ts:126-140) and rows outside the departure lead (G:681, :685-686).
Duplicating Collapse into `./native`, at 10 to 12 h. It creates a second engine on `.collapse` markup that must replace the drop-in plugin by name.

Driving the intrinsic endpoint from a `show.bs.collapse` listener or a microtask. The event fires before the writes (src/browser/Collapse.ts:122), and `awaitTransition` reads `getAnimations()` synchronously inside `show` (src/browser/Collapse.ts:141, :212; src/browser/helpers.ts:924-925), which starts the pixel transition first.
Promoting Bootstrap panels to the top layer from an observer of `.bs.` events. Reconciling an external `hidePopover()` would need a non-cancelable `.bs.` hide or a re-open.

Native hosts that carry `.modal` (the verdict's `dialog.modal`). The Bootstrap engine queries `.modal` at src/browser/Tip.ts:97, src/browser/plugins.ts:216-218 and :227, and src/browser/Modal.ts:180-185.

Claiming every `<dialog>` through a plugin-level `beforetoggle` route (verdict:493-499). It would intercept a third party's script `showModal()` and replay it with the engine's Lock, Trap, and Backdrop.
A `focus` key on `DialogOptions`. `showModal()` refuses outside focus whatever the key says (elements.json, limit d; feas:13).

`::backdrop` as the native scrim in stage B. `awaitTransition` excludes pseudo-element effects (src/browser/helpers.ts:931), so a `::backdrop` fade has no completion signal. The `Backdrop` node stays.
Rewriting the Engine departures lead to admit opt-in rows (verdict:82). The drop-in table stays stage A only, and opt-in differences go to the native table.
Native wire names that reuse Bootstrap's past-tense forms (`shown`, `hidden`, `hidePrevented`). One present-tense word per event (names.md:31) keeps every native name distinct from every `.bs.` name.
